candidates.title: Hapag-Lloyd changes LOLO payment process in Chennai and Ennore
candidates.excerpt: Hapag-Lloyd will change the payment process for Lift-On/Lift-Off (LOLO) services at empty container yards in Chennai and Ennore, India. From 1 November 2026, customers must pay the applicable charges directly to the yard or depot operator when the container is handled. Payments must be made through NEFT or UPI. Cash payments will not be accepted. Customers seeking a tax invoice from the yard or depot operator must provide their company name, full billing address, Goods and Services Tax Identification Number and invoice email address when making the payment. Hapag-Lloyd advised customers to have the required payment and billing information available to avoid disruption during container pick-up or drop-off operations.

candidates.title: Adriatic Gate Container Terminal reaches milestone at port of Rijeka
candidates.excerpt: Adriatic Gate Container Terminal, ICTSI’s operation at the Port of Rijeka in Croatia, has handled four million TEUs since joining the ICTSI Group in 2011, with the milestone reached fifteen years into the partnership and five years after AGCT crossed the two million TEU mark. The achievement reflects sustained growth in container traffic through Croatia’s largest seaport and AGCT’s expanding role as a regional Adriatic gateway connecting global shipping networks with inland markets across Central and Southeast Europe. Much of AGCT’s cargo moves beyond Croatia through rail and road connections to key hinterland markets including Austria, the Czech Republic, Hungary, Serbia and Slovakia. candidates.title: Maersk raises pick-up charges in Madagascar
candidates.excerpt: Maersk will revise its Pick-Up Charge (PIC) at Antananarivo and Toamasina in Madagascar from 1 November 2026. The updated tariffs will apply until further notice. The largest increase will apply at Toamasina, where the charge will double to €30 for both 20-foot and 40-foot containers. Maersk said the revision is intended to align the tariffs with the costs of providing its service solutions at the two locations.

candidates.title: Danaos announces quarterly and special dividends
candidates.excerpt: Danaos Corporation has declared a combined cash distribution of US$6 per common share, comprising its regular quarterly dividend and an extraordinary special dividend. The containership owner declared a quarterly cash dividend of US$1 per share for the three months ended 30 September 2026. Danaos also announced an extraordinary special dividend of US$5 per share. Both dividends will be paid on 22 October 2026 to shareholders of record at the close of business on 13 October 2026.

candidates.title: Maersk extends demurrage free time at Durban Gateway Terminal
candidates.excerpt: Maersk has increased the demurrage free period at Durban Gateway Terminal (DGT) from three to five calendar days. The revised period took effect on 1 October 2026 and will remain in place until further notice. The extension applies exclusively to general-purpose dry and non-operating reefer (NOR) containers. All other demurrage terms and conditions remain unchanged. The measure follows recent operational disruption and congestion at DGT, which previously prompted the terminal to call on shipping lines to consider additional free time and demurrage relief for affected customers.

candidates.title: Greta Shipping joins Maersk’s East Africa feeder service
candidates.excerpt: Greta Shipping is expanding its Middle East, Red Sea and Indian Subcontinent network with four new services, according to Alphaliner. From mid-October, the carrier will join Maersk as a vessel provider on the weekly Salalah–Mogadishu HAX/Musafir Express. Initially, the partners will contribute one vessel each, with capacities of approximately 1,700 TEU and 2,500 TEU. Greta Shipping plans to add a second vessel in January 2027, replacing the tonnage provided by Maersk. In addition, Greta Shipping has launched three standalone services: - The fortnightly Salalah–Khor Fakkan Express (SKX) - The India–Red Sea service (IR), operating every three weeks between Nhava Sheva, Mundra and Port Sudan - The fortnightly India–Oman Service (IOS), connecting Nhava Sheva and Sohar The additions expand Greta Shipping’s coverage across the Middle East, East Africa, the Red Sea and the Indian Subcontinent.

candidates.title: ONE folds Hong Kong regional HQ into Singapore
candidates.excerpt: Ocean Network Express is consolidating its Asian regional management in Singapore, folding its Hong Kong-based East Asia headquarters into a new Asia Pacific operation from April 1, 2027. The Japanese containerline said the new Asia Pacific regional headquarters will combine its current East Asia operation in Hong Kong with the South Asia headquarters already based in Singapore. The enlarged unit will oversee 15 markets, with Louis Tang appointed regional head. ONE is also redrawing responsibility for Africa. Its East, West and South African businesses will move under the carrier’s Dubai regional headquarters, while London will retain responsibility for Europe, the Mediterranean and North Africa. The restructuring alters a regional setup that dates back to ONE’s creation. When NYK, MOL and K Line unveiled their merged container operation in 2017, Singapore was selected as global headquarters, with regional headquarters initially established in Hong Kong, London, Richmond and São Paulo.

candidates.excerpt: U.S. weekly rail traffic totaled 537,397 carloads and intermodal units, up 4.85 compared with the same week a year ago, the Association of American Railroads (AAR) said. Traffic for the week ending September 26 totaled 235,787 carloads, up 3% compared with the same week in 2025, while intermodal volume of 301,610 containers and trailers was 6.3% higher compared to the same week in 2025. Seven of the 10 specific carload commodity groups posted an increase compared with the same week in 2025. They were led by metallic ores and metals, 9.5%; petroleum and related products, 9.4%; and chemicals, 7.2%. Shipments of farm products excluding grain and food fell by 3.3%, followed by coal, 2.1%, and motor vehicles and parts, 1.8%. Coal inventories are up 1.4 million tons since the end of 2025, while domestic consumption was down 11.4% y/y. The naming ceremony was attended by RCL’s senior leadership, Dr. Jamlong Atikul, Chairman of the Board of Directors, Sumate Tanthuwanit, Chairman of the Executive Committee of RCL, and Dr. Twinchok Tanthuwanit, President of RCL, along with industry guests and stakeholders. The three newbuilds are the first in a series of eight container ships being built by RCL at CSSC Huangpu Wenchong Shipbuilding. candidates.excerpt: A BNSF train carrying mixed freight caught fire during a burglary in Riverside, California, Thursday morning. The train was traveling from Los Angeles to Chicago, BNSF told FreightWaves. Firefighters found an open upper container burning on the moving double-stack train. Officials have not identified the items inside or reported any stolen cargo. Riverside dispatchers received the first report at 4:40 a.m. near Chicago Avenue. Early information placed the train heading west from downtown. Crews later located it moving east between Spruce and Columbia streets. Riverside Fire Department deployed 19 firefighters, four engines, one truck and a chief officer. Crews move train for access Access problems prevented crews from reaching the flames at their first location. Incident commanders directed railroad personnel to reposition the equipment farther east. candidates.excerpt: Texmaco Rail Gets Two Orders Worth ₹131.36 Crores Texmaco Rail has bagged two domestic orders worth ₹131.36 crore for wagon manufacturing and supplies. While the smaller contract from TCI must be delivered within 16 weeks, the larger order from its joint venture partner Touax Texmaco is slated for completion by May 2027. Market snapshot: Texmaco Rail & Engineering Limited has secured two separate domestic orders collectively valued at ₹131.36 crore. The mandate comprises a ₹24.48 crore contract from Transport Corporation of India Limited and a ₹106.88 crore related-party contract from Touax Texmaco Railcar Leasing Private Limited. Data Snapshot - Texmaco Rail secured two domestic orders totaling ₹131.36 crore. - The order from Touax Texmaco Railcar Leasing is valued at ₹106.88 crore for the supply of 4 BFNS rakes and 4 brake vans. - The contract from Transport Corporation of India is valued at ₹24.48 crore for the supply of 1 ACT wagon rake and 1 brake van.
